guide_description: One day in Interlaken structured around the town's defining geography: a narrow strip of land between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, with the Bernese Oberland peaks rising on all sides. The day moves from the grand promenade to the heights above town and back down to the waterfront, building a complete picture of why this valley became Europe's mountain tourism capital.

days.cluster_tagline: The classic Bernese Oberland panorama - promenade, summit, and two lakes
days.neighborhood_description: Interlaken sits on the alluvial plain between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz, hemmed in by the Harder Kulm ridge to the north and the Jungfrau massif to the south. The Hoheweg is the grand 19th-century promenade at the center of town, designed so hotel guests could watch the Jungfrau across the Hohematte meadow. Everything in Interlaken is within walking distance of this axis.

morning.notes: Walk the full length of the Hoheweg from Interlaken West station to Interlaken Ost - about 1.5 kilometers - before the tour groups arrive. The Hohematte meadow on the south side is kept permanently open by a 19th-century deed restriction preventing development, preserving the unobstructed view of the Jungfrau. The north side of the promenade retains several grand Belle Epoque hotel facades from the 1860s-1900s tourism boom.

afternoon.notes: Take the funicular from the Interlaken Ost side - the lower station is a five-minute walk north of the main train station through a pedestrian tunnel under the railway. At the summit at 1322 meters, the cantilevered viewing platform extends over the valley and gives a simultaneous view of both lakes and the full Eiger-Monch-Jungfrau ridge. Go before noon when morning light hits the south-facing glacier faces directly; afternoon haze builds quickly in summer.

walk_to_next.to: Lake Brienz waterfront at Interlaken Ost

evening.activity_title: Lake Brienz waterfront at Interlaken Ost
evening.notes: The eastern tip of Lake Brienz - the smaller, less-visited of the two lakes flanking Interlaken - has a gravel shore and a small jetty within walking distance of Interlaken Ost station. The lake is glacier-fed and famously turquoise-green; the color is most saturated in late afternoon light. The Brienzersee promenade runs along the north bank and is almost entirely tourist-free compared to the Hoheweg.

if_time_permits.notes: The 1859 casino and concert hall at the eastern end of the Hoheweg is one of the oldest operating Kursaals in Switzerland. The exterior garden facing the Hohematte is freely accessible - the building's Neo-Gothic turrets and the manicured parterre garden are a precise visual record of what 19th-century Swiss resort architecture looked like before most of it was demolished.

Technically a separate municipality absorbed into greater Interlaken, Unterseen's medieval core on the west bank of the Aare channel predates tourist-era Interlaken by several centuries. The central square with the 1671 church tower is the most-photographed spot in the area when framed against the Jungfrau - position yourself at the south end of the square on Kirchgasse for the alignment.
